mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the 5-year moving average coincides with a decline in 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-period SMA by at least 25 bps in a single month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite persistent rate hikes, or the 5-period SMA never reverts downward within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below the 12-month moving average coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market interprets labor market weakness as a prelude to rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-month moving average by at least 10% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the 12-month moving average never falls below PAYEMS by more than 5%, or SPX 20-day returns remain negative despite repeated labor weakness signals.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds its 4-week moving average by 2% in two consecutive months, it triggers a temporary boost in consumer and business confidence, pushing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns higher.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 4-week SMA by ≥2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 12 such triggers, the average 60-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months reduces expectations of rate hikes, producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: During 20 such episodes, the 20-day forward return mean is negative or equal to the mean of neutral (zero) returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for the first time in three months, it signals labor market tightness that often precedes rate hikes, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% and UNRATE was ≥4.0% in the previous two months
failure_condition: Over 10 such episodes, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (HOUST) above the prior month's level, each exceeding the prior month's by at least 2%, form a momentum signal that increases the probability of positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST[t] > HOUST[t-1] by ≥2% and HOUST[t+1] > HOUST[t] by ≥2%
failure_condition: Across 15 such momentum episodes, the 20-day forward return is never positive in >50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 1% in the same month creates a supply-demand imbalance that increases the likelihood of positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month SMA by ≥1% AND CPIAUCSL < 3-month SMA by ≥1% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 8 such events, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 20% compared to the prior month's level, occurring during a Fed pause, predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to market anticipation of future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average by >20% in a month coinciding with FEDFUNDS < 4.5% for the prior two months
regime_hint: Labor market overheating during Fed pause
failure_condition: During 10 such events, the 20-day forward return mean is not negative (p > 0.05).
